scenario: Discussing a news story with a colleague
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of French

vocabulary.note: often used for a legal 'case' or scandal

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tu as lu l'affaire dont tout le monde parle ? Le dernier rapport est inquiétant.
dialogue.translation: Have you read the case everyone is talking about? The latest report is worrying.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oui, mais malgré les gros titres, les chiffres ne montrent pas une hausse réelle.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but despite the headlines, the figures do not show a real increase.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Cependant, le coût de la vie augmente, surtout dans les grandes villes.
dialogue.translation: However, the cost of living is increasing, especially in big cities.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: C'est vrai, mais il faut développer des moyens pour aider les ménages modestes.
dialogue.translation: That's true, but we need to develop ways to help low-income households.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Grâce à certaines initiatives locales, divers projets ont déjà vu le jour.
dialogue.translation: Thanks to certain local initiatives, various projects have already seen the light of day.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oui, mais il faudrait plus de soutien du gouvernement pour que ça change vraiment.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but more government support would be needed for things to really change.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Absolument. En attendant, on peut discuter de l'impact sur notre travail, non ?
dialogue.translation: Absolutely. In the meantime, we can discuss the impact on our work, right?

key_phrases.phrase: les chiffres ne montrent pas une hausse réelle
key_phrases.translation: the figures do not show a real increase

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: C'est bien. Moi, j'apprends mieux en travaillant en groupe, ça m'aide à mémoriser.
dialogue.translation: That's good. I learn better by working in a group, it helps me memorize.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Tu as raison. Peut-être qu'on pourrait réviser ensemble pour le prochain examen ?
dialogue.translation: You're right. Maybe we could review together for the next exam?

scenario: Discussing a problem and offering solutions
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of French

vocabulary.note: Often used in the pronominal form 's'ennuyer' (to be bored), but here in the sense of 'to bother'.
In informal contexts it can mean 'problem' (e.g., 'avoir des ennuis').
Used both for the advice given (des conseils) and for the body (le conseil).
Followed by an infinitive (essayer de faire qqch).
Avoir raison = to be right; donner raison = to agree with someone.
À mon avis = in my opinion.
Opposite of difficile.
Opposite of facile.
Can be at the beginning or end of the sentence.
Indicates the first step in a sequence.
Used to conclude or express relief.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ça m'ennuie vraiment de ne pas arriver à terminer ce projet.
dialogue.translation: It really bothers me not to be able to finish this project.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Quel est le principal ennui ? Peut-être que le problème vient du manque de temps.
dialogue.translation: What is the main problem? Maybe the problem comes from lack of time.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Oui, tu as raison. Et en plus, je n'ai pas de méthode.
dialogue.translation: Yes, you're right. And besides, I don't have a method.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: À mon avis, il faut d'abord établir une liste des tâches. C'est facile à dire, mais ça aide.
dialogue.translation: In my opinion, first you need to make a list of tasks. It's easy to say, but it helps.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Je trouve ça difficile de tout faire seul. As-tu un conseil ?
dialogue.translation: I find it difficult to do everything alone. Do you have any advice?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Essayer de déléguer une partie du travail. Et enfin, n'oublie pas de faire des pauses.
dialogue.translation: Try to delegate part of the work. And finally, don't forget to take breaks.

key_phrases.translation: It bothers me to... / It annoys me to...

scenario: Comparing two options for a trip
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of French

vocabulary.note: Regular verb of the 2nd group, used to express a choice between options.
Masculine noun, synonym of 'prix' but more formal.
Feminine noun, indicates the total time of something.
Adjective, refers to a trip without stops.
Verb of the 3rd group, often used to talk about plans and forecasts.
Verb of the 1st group, conjugated with 'être' in compound tenses.
Masculine noun, opposite of 'arrivée'.
Masculine noun, often used in plural: 'les bagages'.
Feminine noun, used to compare.
Adjective, attention: it can also mean 'dear' in an affectionate sense.
Adverb, expresses a conclusion or a result after reflection.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Pour notre voyage, il faut choisir entre le train et l'avion.
dialogue.translation: For our trip, we have to choose between the train and the plane.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oui, mais le coût est très différent : le train est moins cher, mais l'avion est plus rapide.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but the cost is very different: the train is cheaper, but the plane is faster.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: C'est vrai. Et la durée du trajet ? L'avion est direct, mais il faut arriver deux heures avant le départ.
dialogue.translation: That's true. And the duration of the trip? The plane is direct, but you have to arrive two hours before departure.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Et avec le train, on peut prévoir un bagage plus lourd sans payer de supplément.
dialogue.translation: And with the train, you can plan heavier luggage without paying extra.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Quelle est la différence de prix totale, alors ?
dialogue.translation: What is the total price difference, then?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Le train coûte 80 euros, l'avion 120 euros. Finalement, le train est plus économique.
dialogue.translation: The train costs 80 euros, the plane 120 euros. In the end, the train is more economical.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: D'accord, prenons le train alors !
dialogue.translation: Okay, let's take the train then!

key_phrases.translation: to choose between X and Y

key_phrases.phrase: quelle est la différence de prix

scenario: Talking about social media habits
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of French

vocabulary.note: Often used to share content on social media.
To post a publication or a photo.
To follow someone on social media.
Person who follows an account.
Often used in plural: les réseaux sociaux.
Posts, photos, videos, etc.
Person with many followers who influences opinions.
Expresses contrast with what was said before.
Indicates something close to a limit.
Used to add an argument: et puis d'ailleurs.
Introduces the positive cause.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tu publies presque tous les jours sur les réseaux sociaux, non ?
dialogue.translation: You post almost every day on social media, right?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oui, j'aime partager des photos, mais je ne suis pas un influenceur.
dialogue.translation: Yes, I like sharing photos, but I'm not an influencer.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Pourtant, tu as beaucoup d'abonnés et ton contenu est très intéressant.
dialogue.translation: However, you have many followers and your content is very interesting.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Merci ! Mais je ne passe pas trop de temps à suivre les autres.
dialogue.translation: Thanks! But I don't spend too much time following others.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Moi, je passe beaucoup de temps sur les réseaux, surtout grâce aux vidéos.
dialogue.translation: I spend a lot of time on networks, especially thanks to videos.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: D'ailleurs, ces vidéos viennent souvent d'ailleurs, mais elles sont amusantes.
dialogue.translation: Moreover, these videos often come from elsewhere, but they are fun.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: C'est vrai, et j'adore partager les meilleurs avec mes amis.
dialogue.translation: That's true, and I love sharing the best ones with my friends.

scenario: Giving a short presentation at work
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of French

vocabulary.note: Used to introduce a topic or a person.
Often used in professional contexts to indicate the goal of a project.
Indicates a group of colleagues.
Key word in the workplace.
Refers to data or results of an activity.
Very common adjective, agrees in gender and number.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Bonjour à tous, je vais vous présenter notre projet actuel.
dialogue.translation: Good morning everyone, I will present our current project to you.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Merci. Quel est l'objectif principal ?
dialogue.translation: Thank you. What is the main objective?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: L'objectif est d'augmenter nos ventes, surtout en Europe.
dialogue.translation: The objective is to increase our sales, especially in Europe.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Et comment va faire l'équipe ?
dialogue.translation: And how will the team do it?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Nous allons analyser les résultats pendant deux semaines, puis nous lancerons une campagne.
dialogue.translation: We will analyze the results for two weeks, then we will launch a campaign.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: C'est important, car le budget est limité.
dialogue.translation: It is important, because the budget is limited.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Exactement. Je vais préparer un résumé pour l'équipe.
dialogue.translation: Exactly. I will prepare a summary for the team.

scenario: Discussing a sport or hobby you follow

vocabulary.note: Used for sports competitions, but also for meetings of various kinds.
Masculine noun; indicates the training session.
Used to talk about skill level or competition level.
Regular -er verb; in the sports context it means 'to be a fan'.
First-group verb; used for victories in competitions or matches.
Third-group verb; opposite of gagner.
Adjective that agrees in gender and number (forte, forts, fortes).

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tu regardes souvent le football ?
dialogue.translation: Do you often watch football?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oui, je supporte l'équipe de Lyon, mais je ne rate jamais un match à la télé.
dialogue.translation: Yes, I support the Lyon team, but I never miss a match on TV.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ils jouent bien cette saison ? Tu penses qu'ils vont gagner le championnat ?
dialogue.translation: Are they playing well this season? Do you think they will win the championship?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: C'est difficile à dire. Ils ont un bon niveau, mais ils perdent parfois des points à domicile.
dialogue.translation: It's hard to say. They have a good level, but they sometimes lose points at home.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Je vois. Et tu vas souvent à l'entraînement pour les voir jouer ?
dialogue.translation: I see. And do you often go to training to watch them play?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oui, pendant l'entraînement, je regarde surtout les jeunes joueurs. Ils courent très vite et sont vraiment forts.
dialogue.translation: Yes, during training I mostly watch the young players. They run very fast and are really strong.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: C'est bien de suivre une équipe de près. Moi, je préfère le tennis, mais je comprends ta passion !
dialogue.translation: It's good to follow a team closely. I prefer tennis, but I understand your passion!
